messages:
release-coordinator: quick pre-deploy check for the 11:30 PT canary — putting together a backout swarming checklist. want confirms on runbook links, pin/unpin ownership, and quick validation steps. threshold: p50 latency >300ms OR errors >1.5% over 2m => consider backout :warning:
emma: ack. i'll be primary contact during the canary window. i can trigger smoke tests and call the rollback if needed.
liam: i'm on pin/unpin control. only liam or release-coordinator to unpin unless prior sign-off.
sre-oncall: runbook link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/backout-v2 (use the section 'canary-surge-unwind'). quick command snippets i'll use if we need to verify kernels/kvcache health:
```
# check runtime pods and restart if stuck
kubectl -n redwood get pods -l app=inference -o wide
# tail realtime errors
kubectl -n redwood logs deploy/inference --since=2m | grep -i error | tail -n 50
```
deploy-bot: deploy queued: canary build 2026.03.11-1189 -> staging -> canary (region: us-west2). preflight checks: config-validated, canary-route-created, metric-alarms-armed.
release-coordinator: decision tree snapshot for this canary: 1) detect: threshold breach OR owner reports 2) confirm: sre-oncall runs quick validation commands 3) mitigate: if infra (pods/kernels) restart nodes; if model/regression -> pin to previous and unroute canary 4) backout: release-coordinator + liam authorize unpin; deploy-bot runs unroute/unpin and roll to previous tag.
emma: for smoke tests i'll run the usual: 10 concurrent requests @ 95% token length, validate semantic hashes and latency histogram. i'll post a short summary in thread within 2m of start.
liam: pin/unpin commands i will use (for audit):
`deploy-bot pin --model inference-rt:2026.03.11-1189 --reason "canary pin"`
`deploy-bot unpin --model inference-rt:2026.03.11-1188 --reason "rollback to stable"`
release-coordinator: note: if we hit one of the auto-alarms, do NOT unpin immediately. confirm in thread and run the quick validation steps first. if SRE confirms infra healthy but latency regresses -> unpin.
sre-oncall: adding a quick fallback to routing policy: set route-weight canary=0 by calling the control-plane API if we need to stop traffic fast. example curl below:
```
curl -X POST https://control-plane.prod.internal/routes/set-weight -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' -d '{"route":"canary","weight":0}'
```
release-coordinator: final checklist before we flip: 1) owners present (emma/liam/sre-oncall) 2) runbook link in pinned messages 3) deploy-bot preflight green 4) monitoring alerts armed 5) commit/rolling-doc updated. i'll pin the runbook link and toggles in this thread now. :white_check_mark:
emma: thanks — will post smoke summary ASAP after canary traffic starts.
liam: i'll be on standby to unpin if we agree. thumbs up to proceed. :+1:
release-coordinator: proceeding to canary in T-minus 7m. everyone standby and keep this thread for comms only.
